newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 13.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW In a move which comes as Deputy Prime Minister and National Party Leader Tim Fischer faces direct attacks on his leadership, many MPs from both the Liberal and National Parties are expected to formally sign their intention to cross the floor today and vote against Prime Minister John Howard's controversial 10-point native title plan. Page 3.

-- In a wage claim equivalent to the average annualised wage rise paid by Australia's big four retail banks last year, the Finance Sector Union is seeking a seven per cent pay rise for more than 23,000 employees at the National Australia Bank, setting a bencmark for enterprise bargaining in the banking industry. Page 3.

-- In evidence to a parliamentary committee last Friday, Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston confirmed that Canadian media company CanWest has been given the go ahead by the Government to retain its 57.5 per cent economic interest in the Ten Netwok, paving the way for a public float of the nation's third television network. Page 5.

-- ARCO's Curragh Queensland Mining Ltd's challenge to the "last on, first off" approach to redundancy has failed before a Full Bench of the Australian Industrial Relations Commission. The company argued that a Coal Industry Award clause specifying the princple discriminated on the basis of race, sex, age and union membership. Page 5.

THE AUSTRALIAN Federal Government sources said last night they were expecting a bitter political battle over Budget moves to increase prescription drug prices. The higher prices will not be covered by the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme safety net, leaving the elderly an chronically ill without any special protection. Page 1.

-- In a move which comes after National Party MPs failed to resolve concerns over the Government's proposed 10-point Wik response, Party Leader and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer was forced to defend his leadership last night after public criticism initiaed by prominent New South Wales backbencher Ian Causley. Page 1.

-- In a move which could see a breakdown of the distinctions between universities and TAFEs, Melbourne's Monash University is understood to be negotiating a ground-breaking arrangement with a Victorian TAFE college which would "feed" successful TAFE students into Monash, Australia's largest university. Page 1.

-- According to a Newspoll conducted for the Australian after Prime Minister John Howard's rebuttal of Independent MP Pauline Hanson's controversial views last week, support for Hanson's One Nation Party has increased from seven to nine per cent, while suppot for the Federal Government is at 40 per cent - the lowest level since last year's election. Page 1.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD As internal problems in the National Party seriously impede Prime Minister John Howard's attempts to sell his second Budget, angry backbenchers vowed yesterday to press ahead with attacks on National Party Leader Tim Fischer over his handling of the contetious Wik native title issue and the Party's failure to influence the Government's policies. Page 1.

-- Royal Prince Alfred Hospital medical board chairman Richard West has described as "inappropriate" plans to shut operating theatres for 10 half-day sessions a week, scale back heart surgery and reduce the number of beds to make up a A$5 million budget overun, saying the move is a "serious threat" to health provision. Page 1.

-- In a move which comes as 600 people gathered at Wyong on the New South Wales Central Coast for the funeral of 18-year-old Scott McCluand, who took his own life last week only a month after his girlfriend committed suicide, parents and mental health expert are pushing the State Government to introduce a suicide counselling program in all high schools. Page 1.

-- Council of Intellectual Disability chairman John Jacobsen told a New South Wales parliamentary committee yesterday nearly 1,000 young disabled people are being forced to live in nursing home with elderly residents because there is nowhere suitable for the to live because State and Federal Governments refuse to fund alternative accommodation for them. Page 3.

THE AGE Speaking at a special joint party meeting yesterday which came amid intense public debate over native title, Pauline Hanson and media ownership, Prime Minister John Howard appealed for Coalition unity ahead of tonight's Budget, telling backbenchers not toallow the Budget to be displaced in the media by other issues. Page 1.

-- Transfield Obayashi is investigating an incident which saw a 26-year-old construction worker fall backwards into a hole on a City Link tunnelling site. It took emergency crews two hours to dig the man out of the three-metre hole, and Obayashi said it would upgrade safety standards if necessary. Page 1.

-- Michael Filips, a 51-year-old HIV-infected man who allegedly had unprotected sex with eight people, three of whom have allegedly contracted the disease, yesterday became the first Victorian to face charges of knowingly spreading the virus. Filips appearedin the Moe Magistrates Court on 304 charges relating to alleged offences committed over seven years. Page 1.

-- In an attempt to prevent possible power cuts in Victoria if the State experiences another heat wave like the one last summer, the Victorian Power Exchange has suggested emergency generators in city buildings could be utilised to help boost supply and ease the burden during peak periods. Page 1.
